description: Manual quarantine list — package+id pairs whose advisory we explicitly trust, despite being flagged by GHSA/OSV. Each exception suppresses the matching incident from compromise checks. Use sparingly; document the reason.

exceptions.reason: Indirect exposure advisory: the SDK only depended on a range that could resolve to the malicious debug@4.4.2, which has its own advisory (GHSA-4x49-vf9v-38px). The SDK versions themselves are not malicious.

Advisory GHSA-658g-p7jg-wx5g covers every @usebruno/cli version below 3.2.0 because of the axios supply-chain incident; bruno itself was not malicious. Flagging every old version would be a false positive.

fsevents 1.0.0 to 1.2.10 fetched a prebuilt binary from cloud storage that a third party reclaimed and abused only in April 2023 (suspended on 2023-04-27). The risk depends on when the package was installed, not on the version: flagging every 1.x install (present in countless old lock files via chokidar 2) would be a false positive for almost everyone. The underlying weakness remains reported as a vulnerability (CVE-2023-45311).

bignum 0.12.2 to 0.13.0 optionally downloaded prebuilt binaries from an S3 bucket that later expired and was claimed by a malicious third party. Same class as fsevents: the risk depends on when, and whether, a prebuilt binary was downloaded, not on the version itself.

The advisory covers <= 1.2.1, but after npm removed the 2017 typosquat (1.0.1, published 2017-07-19) the name passed to a legitimate OpenCV port that published 1.0.0 to 1.2.1 between August and November 2017. The malicious 1.0.1 is kept as a curated incident instead.
